title: The Internet’s Encryption Is Being Rewired Before Quantum Computers Arrive

lines.text: Post quantum security isn't really a cipher problem.
lines.label: INTRO

lines.text: It's an inventory problem, and that changes where you start.
lines.label: INTRO

lines.text: In the next few minutes, we'll cover what the real threat is,
lines.label: INTRO

lines.text: where your encryption is hiding,
lines.label: INTRO

lines.text: how to map it, how to switch safely,
lines.label: INTRO

lines.text: and what it costs to wait.
lines.label: INTRO

lines.text: So first, what are we actually worried about?
lines.label: THE REAL THREAT

lines.text: Future quantum computers could weaken the public key systems we rely on,
lines.label: THE REAL THREAT

lines.text: the systems that let your browser trust a website,
lines.label: THE REAL THREAT

lines.text: and let a device check that an update is genuine.
lines.label: THE REAL THREAT

lines.text: That's why post quantum algorithms were designed to resist them,
lines.label: THE REAL THREAT

lines.text: and the standards for the main replacements already exist.
lines.label: THE REAL THREAT

lines.text: But here's the catch.
lines.label: THE REAL THREAT

lines.text: An algorithm can't protect a system nobody can find.
lines.label: THE REAL THREAT

lines.text: So where does this encryption actually live?
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: Think about the lock on an ordinary shopping website.
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: Before your browser trusts that site, it checks a certificate,
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: and that certificate leans on public key encryption underneath.
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: But it's rarely just one certificate.
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: The site might use several, and the payment service behind it
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: can connect through another dependency you never see.
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: A private network tunnel can rely on the same technology,
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: a software update can carry a signature from another system,
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: and the device receiving that update might be years old.
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: So the takeaway here is simple.
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: Every connection is one more place to inspect,
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: and swapping out one library will never finish the job.
lines.label: WHERE IT HIDES

lines.text: Which brings us to the work itself, making the map.
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: Start by writing down every place public key encryption appears.
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: For each one, note which algorithm sits behind it,
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: which software calls it,
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: what data it's protecting,
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: and which vendors stand between your systems and your users.
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: Then rank everything by how sensitive it is
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: and how hard it would be to replace.
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: Secrets that need to last for years come before short lived messages,
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: and critical services come before convenient internal tools.
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: If that sounds like ordinary software maintenance, it is.
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: The difference is that this time, the locks are hidden.
lines.label: MAP IT

lines.text: Once you know what you have, the next question is how to change it safely.
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: And here, compatibility matters as much as encryption.
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: The new algorithm has to work on real devices,
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: in real browsers and servers,
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: with certificates issued by real vendors,
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: and it has to survive normal business traffic.
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: Because a replacement that breaks your customers isn't ready.
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: So you test before you touch production,
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: you keep a record after every replacement,
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: and you avoid hard coding one algorithm forever.
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: That ability has a name, crypto agility.
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: It means you can change algorithms again without rebuilding everything.
lines.label: SWITCH SAFELY

lines.text: Now, what happens if you skip all of this?
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: Hidden systems turn into blockers right when you need to move.
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: A certificate expires before anyone finds its owner.
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: A vendor needs changes before your team can even respond.
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: An old device rejects the new connection,
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: and suddenly updates stop reaching your customers.
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: An emergency replacement means rushed testing and expensive outages,
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: and when one dependency serves many products, the damage spreads.
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: Customers feel it the only way they can, as broken trust.
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: So the real cost isn't stronger encryption.
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: It's people, testing, vendors and downtime,
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: and every month you wait makes each hidden dependency harder to schedule.
lines.label: THE COST OF WAITING

lines.text: So remember this. Quantum readiness begins with knowing your locks.
lines.label: CLOSE

lines.text: Here's something you can do this week.
lines.label: CLOSE

lines.text: Pick one important service and map it.
lines.label: CLOSE

lines.text: List its certificates, libraries, vendors and data flows,
lines.label: CLOSE

lines.text: and mark the one dependency nobody has tested yet.
lines.label: CLOSE

lines.text: Give that gap an owner and a test plan.
lines.label: CLOSE

lines.text: That small map turns a distant threat into real work.
lines.label: CLOSE

lines.text: Because post quantum security was never a cipher problem.
lines.label: CLOSE
